anomalies.observed: On the CAN BUS sheets, both MCP2515 controllers have their SPI data lines connected opposite to the convention used elsewhere on the board: U8 pin 14 (SI) is labeled CAN_CIPO and pin 15 (SO) is labeled CAN_COPI, and U9 pin 14 (SI) is likewise CAN_CIPO with pin 15 (SO) = CAN_COPI. By contrast the SC16IS752 UART expanders U13/U14 are wired correctly (pin 11 A1/SI = SERIAL_COPI, pin 12 SO = SERIAL_CIPO).
anomalies.expected: Per the board's own SPI naming note, COPI is 'Controller Out, Peripheral In' and CIPO is 'Controller In, Peripheral Out'; the CM4 (controller) drives COPI into the peripheral's SI and reads CIPO from the peripheral's SO. U8/U9 should therefore have SI = CAN_COPI and SO = CAN_CIPO, as U13/U14 do.

evidence.quote: CAN BUS sheet: U8 '14 SI' with net CAN_CIPO, '15 SO' with net CAN_COPI; U9 '14 SI' CAN_CIPO, '15 SO' CAN_COPI (sheets 6-7/10)
Serial sheet: U13/U14 pin 11 'A1/SI' = SERIAL_COPI, pin 12 'SO' = SERIAL_CIPO (sheet 8)
SPI Naming Note: COPI "Controller Out, Peripheral In" CIPO "Controller In, Peripheral Out"

anomalies.impact: The CAN0/CAN1 SPI buses are non-functional: the CM4's output (CAN_COPI) collides with the MCP2515's SO output on the same net, while the CM4's input (CAN_CIPO) is tied to the MCP2515's SI input and never driven. Neither CAN controller can be configured or used, so the isolated CAN0/CAN1 interfaces on J2/J13 — the path to the Odrive motor controllers — would not work.

parsed.summary: Most of the board matches the specification (16 MHz crystals Y1/Y2, LTC4412 U6 + P-MOSFET, TVS arrays D9/D10, WS2812 chain, e-stop buffers U15/U22/U35/U36), but the two MCP2515 CAN controllers U8/U9 have their SPI SI/SO lines swapped relative to the board's own COPI/CIPO convention (as correctly applied to U13/U14), which would break communication with both CAN buses.
